review_notes: I read the whole target file. It has one theorem (coindFunctor_map_shortExact), one instance (coindFunctor_preservesMonomorphisms) and one theorem (coindFunctor_preservesEpimorphisms). It introduces no new structure, definition or class that could compete with a Mathlib concept. The theorem states exactness with Mathlib's Function.Injective, Function.Surjective and Function.Exact, and the other two results use Mathlib's Functor.PreservesMonomorphisms and PreservesEpimorphisms. The file docstring explains why exactness is stated on underlying maps, not as CategoryTheory ShortComplex.ShortExact. It says preserving monos and epis does not give middle exactness, and the supplied category is a subcategory of TopRep. The auxiliary ContCohomology.DiscreteShortExact is only used here and is defined in another file, outside the scope of this review. I did not look for a Mathlib counterpart to it. I found no justified finding under this rubric.
